acceptance: A run with --capture-dir shows why the walk stops at the Google fallback, recorded here.
The cause is fixed in Theseus, in the consumer config, or reported as an OMP regression with evidence; the canary is not weakened to pass.
make omp-candidate-check on a clean develop checkout for the pinned version ends with a result=releasable evidence line, and the daily omp-pin-bump completes without a red state.
context: Handoff prompt for the Theseus session covers diagnosis steps. Spans two repos: canary and broker in joeharris76/theseus, fallback order and policy in BenchBox. A Theseus change needs a release and a re-lock promotion PR.
description: `omp-candidate-check` now runs its live checks (the Namespace crash is fixed in Theseus v0.2.6, locked on develop), and fails one of 27: `live-quota-fallback-walk`. It was observed for 18.16.0 on a clean develop checkout on the owner's Mac (26 pass, 1 fail, no releasable evidence line) and for 18.18.2 in the daily `omp-pin-bump` run 42521407943 (state=red, no candidate PR opened). The check expects the Anthropic Sonnet quota walk to reach `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol` (Theseus `candidate_checks.py` QUOTA_CHAIN_TARGET). BenchBox `.github/oracle-omp-config.yml` lists `google-antigravity/claude-sonnet-5-5` first and GPT second. Both streams reached Google and stopped. The reason is unverified: the run kept no stream capture, and the loopback broker is seeded only with an Anthropic key, so a Google attempt may fail for a reason other than usage-limit. This is not shown to be an OMP regression; it may be a canary expectation, a config mismatch or a broker limitation. Until fixed, the scheduled bump fails red every day and cannot propose a candidate.
